title: Polio took the use of his leg. It didn't take his jump. October 13, 2026.
excerpt: From a coalition government that proved it could last, to a shipyard being built for 200-metre warships, October 13's five stories are about structures - political, institutional, medical, physical - built to hold weight they weren't originally designed for.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is about something built to carry more than it was first asked to - a coalition designed to govern for a full term when that had rarely worked before, a philanthropy led by someone who once ran an entire government aid agency, a military medical model rebuilt for Indian villages, a shipyard expanded to build ships twice the size of what came before, and a leg that carried an athlete to two Paralympic podiums after polio should have ended that possibility entirely.

October 13, 1999: a coalition government was sworn in - and this time, it lasted the full five years

A 70-member coalition ministry was sworn in at Rashtrapati Bhavan, bringing together more than a dozen regional and national parties. It became the first coalition government in India to complete a full five-year term, proving multi-party coordination could sustain stable governance.

He led the US government's global development agency. Now he leads a 110-year-old philanthropy. In 2026, TIME named him to its Philanthropy 100

Dr. Rajiv J. Shah, the first Indian-American president of the Rockefeller Foundation, was named to the TIME100 Philanthropy 2026 list. Before this role he served as the 16th Administrator of USAID from 2010 to 2015 - institutional leadership at the highest level, not a single philanthropic gift.

A 23-year Navy doctor took military medic training and rebuilt it for Indian villages

Dr. Thakor G. Patel, a former US Navy Medical Corps captain, adapted the Navy's Independent Duty Corpsman training into the Sevak Project - training rural Gujarati villagers over roughly two months to provide community healthcare, screening, and chronic disease monitoring where no doctor is nearby.

India just laid the foundation for a shipyard that can build 200-metre warships

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh laid foundation stones for five GRSE and Yantra India Limited expansion projects in West Bengal, anchored by a new shipbuilding hub at Raichak designed to build warships up to 200 metres - more than double what the yard could handle before.

Polio took the use of his leg. It didn't take his jump

Sharad Kumar, left with permanent leg paralysis by childhood polio, took up high jump in 2005 and went on to win bronze at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics and silver at Paris 2024, setting a Paralympic record in his class.

Five stories, one thread: a government built to outlast the usual pattern, a leader whose institutional reach outgrew any single donation, a medical model rebuilt for a context it was never designed for, a shipyard rebuilt to carry twice its old capacity, and a leg rebuilt into something that could clear 1.88 metres. Nothing here stayed at its original scale.
